classification.difficultyReason: The task is heavily scaffolded: parts a and b state each step. Part a is a direct conversion of red:yellow to a fraction (1/3 and 2/5), with no part-whole step. Part b is a routine common-denominator conversion of thirds and fifths, so the student needs only the LCD of 15 and two equivalent fractions. Part c needs one interpretive step, reading the larger fraction (6/15 > 5/15) as more red per yellow, and the answer follows straight from b. The hardest demand is therefore a linked ratio-to-fraction comparison, which is more than the direct reading of ratios and fractions in p7-q7. It stays below p61-q13, which asks the student to convert a percentage and a fraction and build a three-part ratio unprompted.
